mode achieved: static review only (a Stryker run was in progress, so no Jest, Stryker, tsc, ESLint or pnpm); read in full all 36 in-scope test and helper files, src/window.test.setup.ts and jest.config.js, the 14 production files they cover, stryker.config.json, eslint.config.js:38-52, src/app/_layout.tsx, and the RNTL, jest-circus and expo-router sources behind three matcher and hook-order claims; ran 8 counting probes (grep and python3 over the 37 in-scope files).
verdict: 1 blocker, 4 major, 4 nit. No assertion is vacuous today: toHaveTextContent is exact by default [Source: node_modules/@testing-library/react-native/dist/matches.js:8-15], toHaveStyle({k: undefined}) really tests absence [Source: node_modules/@testing-library/react-native/dist/matchers/to-have-style.js:11-14], and the "no network call" checks fail through onUnhandledRequest 'error'. But retyped literals make 8 absence checks go vacuous after a routine data or copy edit.

🔴 blocker  Demo fixture values are retyped as literals in 205 lines of 23 test files, and 7 absence checks keyed on them go silently vacuous after a routine fixture edit
- key: src/mocks/fixtures#retyped-fixture-values
- where: 205 lines in 23 of the 37 in-scope files; 13 of those 23 import the fixture module they retype (probe: `cd apps/metis && grep -rnE "Northwind|Client Delivery|Meridian CGI|Contoso|Spring Catalogue|Creative Studio|Digital Products|Acme Holdings|Nadia R\.|creative-studio|digital-products|meridian-cgi-campaign|northwind-showroom-vr|spring-catalogue-renders|Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh|api\.metis\.test" src/core src/platform src/mocks src/shell --include='*.test.*' | wc -l` printed 205). By value: 'creative-studio' 78 lines in 20 files, 'meridian-cgi-campaign' 37 in 15, 'Creative Studio' 22 in 9, 'Nadia R.' 13 in 5, 'Northwind Furniture Co' 11 in 7. Examples: src/shell/TopBar.test.native.tsx:11-17 and :27 (crumbs, user and bell count retyped); src/shell/model.workspace.test.ts:27-66 (the whole creativeStudio tree retyped); src/shell/Shell.narrow.test.native.tsx:38-50 (fixture badge counts baked into 'My focus 9' and 'Approvals 3'); src/shell/ProjectHeader.test.helper.tsx:17 and src/shell/model.header.test.ts:14 ('Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh' instead of meridian.timeZone); the API base URL in 6 files (src/core/api/client.test.ts:8, src/mocks/handlers.test.ts:9, src/platform/mocks.test.native.ts:5, src/platform/config.test.ts:4, src/shell/Shell.test.native.tsx:144, src/shell/useShell.test.native.ts:66) beside apiConfig.
- why: Mechanism: the fixture modules export objects but no ids or derived names, and the mock handler keeps its ids private and retypes them itself (src/mocks/handlers.ts:12, :14-20, :22), so every test author copied the literal from the plan block. Cost: a demo-data edit is a hand edit across unit tests, e2e and scripts (brief fact 1: 13 files). Worse, 7 absence checks use a retyped literal as their only key while their positive twin sits in another test: src/shell/Shell.test.native.tsx:152 and :164 (twin :128), src/shell/Shell.narrow.test.native.tsx:96 (twins :130, :148, :238) and :181 (twins :189, :215), src/shell/TopBar.test.native.tsx:187-189 (twins :169, :178). After a rename the twins go red and get fixed; the absence checks keep passing whatever renders, because nothing can match a name that no longer exists.
- fix: add src/mocks/fixtures/index.ts exporting the ids and names tests need, read off the objects (`export const USER = creativeStudio.user`, `export const MERIDIAN_REF = creativeStudio.tree[0]!.programs[0]!.projects[0]!`), and make handlers.ts and the HOME of platform/config.ts use it; in tests replace the literals with `USER.name`, `meridian.project.client`, `meridian.timeZone`, `apiConfig.baseUrl`, and key every absence query on the same expression as its positive twin; give the pure model tests (src/shell/model*.test.ts) a small builder (`shellWith({ tree: [...] })`) so each expected value is visibly derived from input written in the same test.
- approach-changing: yes, it adds a test-data accessor layer that every plan C screen test must import from.
- trigger: rename the demo user at src/mocks/fixtures/shell.ts:31 and fix the three tests that go red (Shell.test.native.tsx:128, Shell.narrow.test.native.tsx:189 and :215); a later regression that draws the avatar while the shell is loading or after a 404 then passes Shell.test.native.tsx:152 and :164, which still look for 'Nadia R.'.
- guard-bypass: coverage and mutation judge only production files, no lint rule links a test literal to the fixture, and a negative query on a string that cannot render passes by construction.
- design: yes, a fixture accessor module plus a lint rule or review checklist item that rejects retyped fixture ids and names in *.test.* files.

🟡 major  Shell copy is retyped in 152 test literals across 12 shell test files, while the dictionary is read through STRINGS in only 13 places
- key: src/shell/strings#retyped-copy-in-tests
- where: quoted literals equal to a value of src/shell/strings/en.ts: 152 hits, 53 distinct values: model.sidebar.test.ts 29, Shell.narrow.test.native.tsx 27, Sidebar.test.native.tsx 19, NotBuilt.test.native.tsx 16, model.header.test.ts 14, ProjectHeader.test.native.tsx 12, ProjectHeader.narrow.test.native.tsx 9, TopBar.test.native.tsx 8, Sidebar.tree.test.native.tsx 8, Shell.test.native.tsx 6, Shell.safeArea.test.native.tsx 2, model.workspace.test.ts 2; lookups through `STRINGS.<locale>.`: 13 in 3 files (probe: python3 comparing every quoted literal of the in-scope tests with every en.ts value of 3 or more characters without a placeholder; the self-contained fake dictionaries of src/core/i18n/*.test.ts excluded). Vietnamese copy retyped: 9 vi.ts values (src/shell/NotBuilt.test.native.tsx:121-134, src/shell/Shell.test.native.tsx:173-176) plus filled templates (src/shell/TopBar.test.native.tsx:235, src/shell/model.workspace.test.ts:111, src/shell/ProjectHeader.test.native.tsx:226-228, which repeat model.header.test.ts:95-97). Filled English copy retyped whole: 'My focus 9' 6 times, 'Baseline v1 ·' 5, 'PM Nadia R.' 4, 'stage 3 of 6' 4. One file mixes both styles: TopBar.test.native.tsx:31 types 'Open menu' beside `strings={STRINGS.en}` while :231 uses `vi.search`. The menu error sentence is declared twice (src/shell/Sidebar.test.native.tsx:13, src/shell/Shell.test.native.tsx:32).
- why: a copy edit by product breaks up to 12 files; and src/shell/Shell.narrow.test.native.tsx:95 (`within(rail).queryByText('Investment')`) has its only positive twin in another test (:131), so after a label edit :131 goes red and gets fixed while :95 silently stops guarding "planned items stay out of the rail". The other copy-keyed absence checks (Sidebar.test.native.tsx:191, Sidebar.tree.test.native.tsx:88-89) have their twin in the same test, so they fail loudly.
- fix: per file `const t = STRINGS.en` and query the key: TopBar.test.native.tsx:31 `menu={{ label: t.menu.open, open: false, onPress: jest.fn() }}`; Shell.narrow.test.native.tsx:95 `queryByText(t.later.investment)`; Sidebar.test.native.tsx:13 and Shell.test.native.tsx:32 `const ERROR = t.sidebar.menuError`; NotBuilt.test.native.tsx:121-134 `STRINGS.vi.page.notBuilt` and siblings. Keep each filled template as a literal golden only in the model test that owns it (model.header.test.ts, model.sidebar.test.ts) and let component tests query the model output (`headerOf().stage`); do not rebuild templates with interpolate() inside a test, that reimplements the code under test.
- approach-changing: no, a mechanical rewrite onto an object that already exists.
- trigger: change src/shell/strings/en.ts:40 later.investment to 'Investments' and fix the one red line (Shell.narrow.test.native.tsx:131); a later regression that puts Investment into the tablet rail passes :95.
- guard-bypass: src/shell/strings/strings.test.ts audits en against vi only; nothing checks where tests take copy from.

🟡 major  Test titles, comments and failure messages are Vietnamese (213 of 222 titles), and 14 titles start with the plan id 'D-19'
- key: src/shell#vietnamese-test-language
- where: the 37 in-scope files hold 460 lines with the brief's diacritic class; titles: 213 of 222 describe, test and test.each titles (the 9 English ones are names such as describe('TopBar')); comment lines: 155 of 157 (probe: python3 over the 37 files with the character class of brief fact 3); 14 titles start with 'D-19 ' (src/shell/ProjectHeader.narrow.test.native.tsx:26, :40, :56; src/shell/Shell.narrow.test.native.tsx:57 to :248, nine titles; src/shell/Shell.safeArea.test.native.tsx:35, :54); 31 lines cite 'D-19', a ruling id or a spec section; thrown messages in Vietnamese at src/mocks/handlers.test.ts:106 and :131; two orphan comments describe tests that moved to another file (src/shell/ProjectHeader.test.native.tsx:234, src/shell/Shell.narrow.test.native.tsx:266-267).
- why: Jest prints the title and the thrown message on failure, so a developer of the agency cannot tell which behaviour broke or grep for it, and 'D-19' points into a Vietnamese plan nobody there will read; every test file copied as a template for plan C carries the language with it.
- fix: rewrite titles as English behaviour statements (Shell.narrow.test.native.tsx:57 becomes 'tablet: an icon rail replaces the sidebar, each link is a named button'), drop the 'D-19' prefixes and ruling ids or replace each with a one-line English why, translate the two Error messages, delete the two orphan comments. Once copy comes from STRINGS.vi and NATIVE_NAMES (finding above), test files need no diacritics at all, so the guard can be flat: a custom rule in eslint-rules/ that reports the diacritic class in comments, test titles and string literals, allowlisting src/**/strings/vi.ts, src/core/i18n/locale.ts and the self-contained i18n tests src/core/i18n/*.test.ts.
- approach-changing: no, it applies the default convention of the brief.
- trigger: a plan C developer copies Shell.narrow.test.native.tsx as the template for a new screen; CI later fails with 'D-19 tablet: the count at the button corner, red for an alert; ...' and nobody on the team can read which behaviour broke.
- guard-bypass: no lint rule or gate checks the language of titles, comments or messages (brief fact 3: 2,220 lines repo-wide).
- design: yes, the language lint rule with its allowlist.

🟡 major  Mirror tests restate the code under test: 125 style assertions copy the *.styles.ts files and six tests copy constant tables, so they agree with a wrong value by construction
- key: src/shell#mirror-tests
- where: 125 toHaveStyle calls in 9 shell test files (probe: grep count over the in-scope files); src/shell/TopBar.test.native.tsx:53-61 repeats src/shell/TopBar.styles.ts:8-16 key for key; src/shell/Sidebar.test.native.tsx:96-106, titled "matches the wireframe", compares contentContainerStyle by exact object. Constant tables: src/core/routes.test.ts:3-52 (ROUTES and SCREENS retyped, 44 lines), src/core/api/shell.test.ts:16-34 (NAV_CODES), src/mocks/handlers.test.ts:63-73 (SCENARIOS), src/platform/config.test.ts:3-9 (apiConfig, HOME), src/core/i18n/locale.test.ts:3-10 (LOCALES, NATIVE_NAMES), src/shell/strings/strings.test.ts:11-14; and src/core/routes.test.ts:86-92 asserts a value the test assigned two lines above (a type check written as a runtime assertion).
- why: in-sample: expected values and code were copied from the same plan block, so a wrong value passes; these tests catch accidental edits only and double every intended change. Measured today, no live defect: all 22 SCREENS entries match the `order` of wireframes/manifest.json (probe: python3 lookup, 22 of 22), and the TopBar values match wireframes/assets/wireframe.css:39, :42, :43 (gap 12, search width 300, padding 6 and 10, bell 30) against src/design-system/tokens.ts:91, :111, :107. No gate needs the style mirrors: stryker.config.json excludes `src/**/*.styles.ts` from mutation, and coverage of a StyleSheet module is met by importing it.
- fix: keep style assertions that encode a state or rule (active versus inactive item, touch target on phone versus desktop, safe-area insets, error state) and delete static copies of a styles file, or generate their expected values from wireframe.css the way scripts/gen-tokens.mjs generates tokens from brand/tokens.css; replace the constant mirrors with properties that can fail: every SCREENS value is an `order` present in wireframes/manifest.json, every NAV_CODES entry is a Destination or a key of en.later; delete the SCENARIOS, HOME and STRINGS mirrors (scenarioOf, the handler tests and the dictionary audit already test their behaviour); turn routes.test.ts:86-92 into a `// @ts-expect-error` case as src/core/i18n/dictionary.test.ts:7-12 does.
- approach-changing: yes, it decides that static visual conformance is checked against the wireframe (e2e or generated values), not by copying styles into Jest.
- trigger: plan C adds a destination and copies its screen number from the plan with a typo; the author retypes the same number into routes.test.ts; the not-built page shows the wrong screen and every test stays green.
- guard-bypass: a mirror has no input other than the constant itself, so it can never disagree with it.
- design: yes, a rule for what a component test may assert about style plus a non-mirror oracle for wireframe values.

🟡 major  The test harness is copy-pasted per file: fake-timer reset, MSW lifecycle, module mocks, model builders, and two hand-made replicas of the root layout
- key: src/window.test.setup.ts#copied-harness
- where: a nested `afterEach(() => jest.useRealTimers())` in 10 in-scope files (11 calls) with its 3-line comment copied 8 times (src/shell/TopBar.test.native.tsx:40-46, src/shell/NotBuilt.test.native.tsx:34-40), 16 files repo-wide; the MSW lifecycle in 6 files (src/core/api/client.test.ts:11-18, src/mocks/handlers.test.ts:10-14, src/shell/Shell.test.native.tsx:20-30, src/shell/Shell.narrow.test.native.tsx:22-33, src/shell/Shell.safeArea.test.native.tsx:13-23, src/shell/useShell.test.native.ts:13-20); the storage factory mock in 5 files; the fingerOnly getter mock in 2 (src/shell/ProjectHeader.narrow.test.native.tsx:9-17, src/shell/Shell.narrow.test.native.tsx:14-19); HIDDEN in 3; identical builders: headerOf (src/shell/ProjectHeader.test.helper.tsx:10-21) and header (src/shell/model.header.test.ts:7-18), sidebar (src/shell/model.sidebar.test.ts:9-19 and src/shell/model.workspace.test.ts:8-18), modelOf plus mount (src/shell/Sidebar.test.native.tsx:18-42 and src/shell/Sidebar.tree.test.native.tsx:17-32), clone, broken and withRows (src/core/api/overview.test.ts:6-16 and :206-210, src/core/api/overview.presence.test.ts:10-20 and :39-42); the root layout copied by hand in src/shell/Shell.test.native.tsx:35-51 and src/shell/Shell.test.helper.tsx:20-40 (different route sets) instead of the real src/app/_layout.tsx:20-26.
- why: mechanism: `'max-lines': ['error', 300]` (eslint.config.js:49) applies to test files too, so a full file is split and the split copies its helpers (src/core/api/overview.presence.test.ts:5 says so). Cost: each new screen test starts by copying about 20 lines; a forgotten timer reset costs about 5 s per test under Stryker by the repo's own comment (TopBar.test.native.tsx:40-42); a change to _layout.tsx is invisible to the replicas while src/app/** is outside coverage (jest.config.js:75), so no unit test runs the real provider stack.
- fix: (1) one line in src/window.test.setup.ts, `afterEach(() => jest.useRealTimers())`, then delete the 10 describe wrappers: jest-circus runs the afterEach hooks of one block in declaration order and the setup file registers its hook before RNTL registers auto-cleanup on import [Source: node_modules/jest-circus/build/utils.js:188-205; node_modules/@testing-library/react-native/dist/index.js:20-30] (NOT RUN: Stryker run in progress; confirm with `pnpm -C apps/metis exec jest src/shell`); (2) src/test/server.ts exporting `useMockServer(scenario = 'default')` that registers the four hooks and calls `server.use` inside beforeEach, as the current comment requires for Stryker; (3) src/platform/__mocks__/storage.ts so each file writes only `jest.mock('../platform/storage')`; (4) move headerOf, sidebar, modelOf and the overview clone helpers into *.test.helper.ts files beside their subject, as fonts.test.helper and Select.test.helper already do; (5) export the provider stack (LocaleProvider around Shell) from src/shell, use it in _layout.tsx and in mountShell, and delete the replica in Shell.test.native.tsx.
- approach-changing: yes, it fixes the harness every plan C screen test starts from.
- trigger: a plan C screen test omits the nested afterEach; under Stryker each of its tests waits out RNTL cleanup for 5 s, for every mutant whose per-test coverage includes it.
- guard-bypass: nothing enforces the reset; it depends on each author copying a Vietnamese comment.
- design: yes, a shared test-harness module and a rule that a split test file imports its builders instead of copying them.

💭 nit  44 assertions walk the host tree (parent, children, sibling index), so a wrapper View with no user-visible effect breaks them
- key: src/shell#host-tree-walks
- where: 44 lines in 8 files (probe: grep of `\.(parent|children)\b` over the in-scope files); src/shell/Sidebar.test.native.tsx:27-33 depends on "RNTL draws ScrollView as RCTScrollView wrapping a View" and drives :269 and :278; src/shell/TopBar.test.native.tsx:84-86 checks that earlier crumbs are raw strings and the last an object; src/shell/Sidebar.test.native.tsx:111-115 finds the spacer by sibling index; src/shell/Shell.narrow.test.native.tsx:87 reads `registry.children[0]`; src/shell/ProjectHeader.test.native.tsx:44-49 styles `title.parent?.parent`.
- why: these tests go red on refactors that change nothing for the user (false failures), and plan C will copy the technique.
- fix: put a testID on the element whose style or count matters (spacer, glyph, title block, scroll content) and query it directly; for "only the last crumb is bold" assert the style of each crumb text instead of child types.
- approach-changing: no, local rewrites.

💭 nit  The stale-response test of useShell uses a 100 ms real sleep as its oracle
- key: src/shell/useShell.test.native.ts#sleep-oracle
- where: src/shell/useShell.test.native.ts:82-86
- why: an absence-of-action check ("a late answer for the old workspace does not overwrite"): the test proves the old response left MSW (:71-75), then waits 100 ms; on a loaded machine the client's continuation (body read, zod parse, then) can land after the assertion, so the test passes even with the guard at src/shell/useShell.ts:18 deleted. It does go red on deletion today (mutation score 100 per the brief), so this is a latent false pass, not a live one.
- fix: await the old call's own promise instead of sleeping: `import * as client from '../core/api/client'`, before mounting `const call = jest.spyOn(client, 'getShell')`, then `await act(async () => { release(); await call.mock.results[0]?.value })`; the hook's then was registered first, so it has run when the await resumes. Spying needs the transpiled useShell to read getShell from the module object at call time [Unverified - confirm before applying]; NOT RUN: Stryker run in progress, confirm with `pnpm -C apps/metis exec jest src/shell/useShell.test.native.ts` and by deleting the `if (current)` of useShell.ts:18 (expect red).
- approach-changing: no, one test.

💭 nit  Platform early returns let a test pass with zero assertions on the Android project
- key: src/shell/TopBar.test.native.tsx#platform-early-return
- where: src/shell/TopBar.test.native.tsx:243 (`if (Platform.OS !== 'ios') return`: the whole test is empty on Android), :201-205 (half the test skipped on iOS), :220
- why: Jest reports the Android run of the test at :242 as passed with no assertion, which inflates the test count, and the iOS action-sheet copy (topbar.cancel) would stay unguarded behind a green report in any run without the iOS project.
- fix: `const iosOnly = Platform.OS === 'ios' ? test : test.skip` and `iosOnly('...', ...)` so Android reports it as skipped, or move it to TopBar.test.ios.tsx as src/platform/fonts.test.ios.ts already does; add `beforeEach(() => expect.hasAssertions())` to src/window.test.setup.ts so any assertion-free test fails (NOT RUN: Stryker run in progress).
- approach-changing: no, local.

💭 nit  Program counts are asserted anywhere on screen, not in their own row
- key: src/shell/Sidebar.tree.test.native.tsx#count-not-bound
- where: src/shell/Sidebar.tree.test.native.tsx:90-91 (`getByText('2')`, `getByText('1')`); rendering at src/shell/Sidebar.tsx:186
- why: if the Sidebar drew each program's count beside the wrong program (Northwind 1, Contoso 2) this test still passes; src/shell/model.workspace.test.ts:35 and :53 pin the model, not the binding of a count to its row.
- fix: give each program row a testID in Sidebar.tsx and assert `within(screen.getByTestId(<Northwind row>)).getByText(<count from the model>)`.
- approach-changing: no, one assertion.
